Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Environment: Warm temperatures (24–30°C), high humidity, rainfall and overhead irrigation favor disease development.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Spread: Spread through infected seeds, rain splash, irrigation water, contaminated tools and human handling.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Description: Bacterial Spot is a serious bacterial disease of tomato that affects leaves, stems and fruits. Severe infection causes premature leaf drop, reducing fruit quality and yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small water-soaked spots appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Dark brown lesions enlarge and merge, causing yellowing.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves dry and fall prematurely. Fruits develop raised scabby lesions.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually appear within 5–10 days after infection.

Treatment: Use copper mixed with mancozeb for improved effectiveness.
Recommended_Actions: Apply preventive copper sprays during humid weather.

Tomato___Early_blight.Environment: Warm temperatures (24–29°C), high humidity and frequent rainfall promote infection.
Tomato___Early_blight.Spread: Fungal spores spread through wind, rain splash, contaminated soil and infected plant debris.
Tomato___Early_blight.Description: Early Blight is one of the most common tomato diseases. It first attacks older leaves and gradually spreads upward, reducing photosynthesis and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small brown spots appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Concentric target-like rings develop on lesions.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves die, stems become infected and fruits develop dark lesions.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease develops within 7–14 days under favorable conditions.

Tomato___Late_blight.Environment: Cool temperatures (10–22°C), high humidity (>90%) and prolonged rainfall.
Tomato___Late_blight.Spread: Airborne spores spread rapidly by wind, rain splash and infected plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.Description: Late Blight is one of the most destructive tomato diseases. It spreads rapidly during cool, wet weather and can destroy entire fields within a few days if unmanaged.

Age_Cycle.Moderate: Brown lesions enlarge rapidly with white fungal growth underneath.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Entire plant collapses and fruits rot quickly.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease may spread across a field within 3–7 days under ideal conditions.

Prevention: Monitor weather forecasts for blight risk.
Recommended_Actions: Take immediate action after first symptoms.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Environment: High humidity (>85%), poor ventilation and temperatures between 20–27°C.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Spread: Airborne spores spread through wind, splashing water and contaminated plant material.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Description: Leaf Mold mainly affects greenhouse and protected tomato cultivation. It begins on older leaves and can significantly reduce photosynthesis and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Pale yellow spots appear on the upper leaf surface.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Olive-green to gray fungal growth develops underneath the leaves.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves curl, dry and fall prematurely.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Environment: Warm (20–25°C), humid weather with frequent rainfall.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Spread: Rain splash, irrigation water, contaminated tools and infected crop debris.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Description: Septoria Leaf Spot primarily attacks tomato foliage. Although fruits are rarely infected directly, severe defoliation reduces fruit size, quality and yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small circular gray spots appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Dark borders form around lesions and tiny black fruiting bodies develop.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves turn yellow, dry and drop prematurely.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Environment: Hot, dry weather with low humidity.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Spread: Mites move between plants by wind, equipment, workers and infested plant material.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny sap-sucking pests that weaken tomato plants by feeding on leaf tissue, reducing photosynthesis and causing premature leaf loss.

Age_Cycle.Early: Tiny yellow speckles appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Fine webbing develops and leaves become bronze.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves dry completely and plants become weak.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Population can increase dramatically within 7–10 days in warm conditions.

Tomato___Target_Spot.Environment: Warm (25–30°C), humid weather with prolonged leaf wetness.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Spread: Wind-borne spores, rain splash, infected crop debris and contaminated equipment.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Description: Target Spot is a fungal disease that causes circular lesions on tomato leaves and fruits. Severe infection results in premature defoliation and reduced fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small brown circular spots appear on older leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions enlarge with concentric rings resembling a target.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large areas of leaf tissue die, causing heavy defoliation.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease progresses within 7–14 days under favorable conditions.

Treatment: Apply fungicides at the first sign of disease.
Recommended_Actions: Apply preventive fungicides during humid weather.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Environment: Warm climates with high whitefly populations.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Spread: Transmitted primarily by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus is a highly destructive viral disease that causes severe stunting, curled leaves and drastically reduced fruit production.
Cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus infection

Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaves become yellow and plants become stunted.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Flower drop and little or no fruit production.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually appear 2–3 weeks after infection.

Treatment: There is no cure for infected plants.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Environment: Can occur under a wide range of environmental conditions.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Spread: Mechanical transmission through contaminated hands, tools, clothing and infected plant material.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Description: Tomato Mosaic Virus causes mosaic patterns, leaf distortion and reduced plant vigor. It spreads easily through handling and contaminated equipment.

Age_Cycle.Early: Light and dark green mosaic patterns appear on leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Leaves become distorted and plants grow slowly.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Reduced fruit size and poor yield.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms develop within 10–14 days after infection.

Prevention: Avoid handling plants after tobacco products.

Tomato___healthy.Environment: Well-drained fertile soil, balanced nutrition, adequate sunlight and proper irrigation.
Tomato___healthy.Description: The uploaded tomato leaf shows no visible signs of disease or pest infestation. The plant appears healthy.

Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth under proper management.
